paragraphs: Approaches to mitigation of hydrogen sulfide during anaerobic digestion process – a review
Introduction

Several studies have specified the level of hydrogen sulfide, which microorganisms can tolerate in the digester treating substrate rich in protein. From this study, it is proposed that H2S can be removed firstly by limiting the level of H2S before the digestion process (Pre-digestion), secondly by altering the concentration of H2S during the AD process to ensure the optimization process of the materials required for the purification of the raw biogas produced after the process (During digestion), and lastly is the removal process at the end of the AD process (Post-digestion).
